senses.definition: To change in appearance or slowly break down from being outside in the sun, wind, or rain.

examples.en: The stone steps have weathered after centuries of rain.
examples.vi: Các bậc đá đã bị mòn sau nhiều thế kỷ mưa gió.

examples.en: Paint helps prevent wood from weathering too quickly.
examples.vi: Sơn giúp ngăn gỗ không bị xuống màu quá nhanh.

senses.vi: mòn vì thời tiết; phơi nắng phơi sương; làm mòn

thesaurus.definition: face and withstand with courage
cause to slope
sail to the windward of
change under the action or influence of the weather

vi_block: Dầm mưa dãi gió; để nắng mưa làm hỏng; phơi nắng phơi sương.
Thừa gió vượt qua, căng buồm vượt qua (một mũi đất); vượt qua (cơn bão).
Vượt qua, chiến thắng.
Làm giả sắc cũ, làm giả nước cũ.
Mòn, rã ra, đổi màu (vì gió mưa).

wiktionary.gloss: To expose to the weather, or show the effects of such exposure, or to withstand such effects.

examples:
April 18, 1850, Frederick William Robertson, An Address Delivered to the Members of the Working Man's Institute
You will weather the difficulties yet.
wiktionary.gloss: To sustain the trying effect of; to bear up against and overcome; to endure; to resist.
To break down, of rocks and other materials, under the effects of exposure to rain, sunlight, temperature, and air.
To cause (rocks) to break down by crushing, grinding, and/or dissolving with acids.

examples: to weather a cape    to weather another ship
wiktionary.gloss: To pass to windward in a vessel, especially to beat 'round.

examples: Joshua weathered a collision with a freighter near South Africa.
wiktionary.gloss: To endure or survive an event or action without undue damage.
To place (a hawk) unhooded in the open air.
To rain; to storm.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English weder, wedir, from Old English weder, from Proto-West Germanic *wedr, from Proto-Germanic *wedrą, from Proto-Indo-European *wedʰrom (=*we-dʰrom), from *h₂weh₁- (“to blow”). Cognates

thesaurus.definition: towards the side exposed to wind

examples: weather side, weather helm
wiktionary.gloss: Facing towards the flow of a fluid, usually air.

idioms.gloss: Used to inquire about the weather.
ill or gloomy, especially from a cold or flu.
To reach the end of a very difficult situation without too much harm or damage.
to maintain a background awareness of something; to remain alert to changes without it occupying one's full attention.
To overcomplicate (something); to make (things) appear worse than they are.
Asked to tall people or someone who is at a high vantage point, either literally or metaphorically.
To make progress only with difficulty.
To gain an advantage or accomplish a purpose against opposition.
To be extraordinarily effective, especially when in a position of authority.
To chit-chat; to shoot the breeze.

phrasal_verbs.gloss: To endure all the way; to hold out against till the end.

blocks.etymology: First use appears c. 1850 in Pennsylvania, a calque of German feucht hinter den Ohren. From the drying of amniotic fluid of a baby after birth, specifically a newborn farm animal, whose ears are the last to dry, partly because it is licked dry by its mother everywhere else. Alternative forms also derive from German.

wiktionary.gloss: Inexperienced; just beginning; immature (especially in judgment).
A path in spacetime, especially that traversed by an elementary particle from its creation to its destruction.
